article.name: Holographic
article.summary: Holographic is a local SQLite memory provider for Hermes Agent. It stores versioned facts and entity links, and combines multilingual full-text matching, entity-aware recall, trust weighting, and optional holographic vector similarity. This review describes current source behavior; no runtime quality or performance was measured.

who_what.text: The catalog-listed repository is NousResearch/hermes-agent. Current official Hermes documentation says Holographic moved out of core into a catalog plugin maintained by itpartypattaya; the maintained plugin README identifies the standalone repository as the provider that shipped in Hermes. The active implementation reviewed here is that catalog plugin, while the catalog-listed Hermes repository is retained as the roster locator.

The maintained README describes a local SQLite provider with no required API key, network access, or model call by default. Optional embedding and reranking integrations can send fact/query text to configured endpoints; these are separate opt-in paths.

architecture.text: The central MemoryStore keeps current facts in SQLite, with content, category, tags, trust score, retrieval/helpfulness counts, timestamps, and an optional HRR vector. FTS5 indexes content and tags; triggers update the index when indexed text changes. Entity and fact_entities tables link names/aliases to facts; optional per-fact embeddings and fact-version/history tables extend the store.

The plugin is organized into a store and supporting modules for retrieval, HRR encoding, entity resolution, version history, optional embeddings/reranking, and the optional experience journal. Hermes installs it as an external memory provider, alongside rather than replacing Hermes built-in MEMORY.md and USER.md stores.

Holographic's configuration supports profile, user, chat, and thread scope modes. The README describes separate local database files for scope identities and says a missing identity prevents reads and writes in the relevant modes. Hermes documentation also describes local storage providers as profile-isolated. These are documented boundaries, not cross-scope test results.

behavior.text: Write: fact_store add records a fact and optional category, tags, entities, validity date, origin, and source metadata. Store code keeps an FTS index and resolves/links entities; writes can also create HRR encodings when NumPy is available. The README documents opt-in turn extraction and mirroring of built-in memory writes; both are separate automatic capture paths.

Update and correction: the action surface includes update/change/correct/revert/merge and history operations. Version history retains prior versions and valid-time bounds; origin and source metadata are attached to versions. Similar facts and possible conflicts are returned as advisories for the agent to decide, rather than automatically proving or reconciling a contradiction.

Delete and forgetting: remove/forget deletes a fact and its dependent versions and records keyed digests rather than the forgotten text; entity deletion also leaves keyed tombstones and removes links. The documented controls are local to this SQLite store; the inspected sources do not establish erasure from backups or external copies.

Retrieval: keyword candidates come from FTS5; multilingual stemming, token/character processing, term overlap, Jaccard-style similarity, entity recall, trust weighting, optional HRR similarity, and optional reranking contribute to selection. Before-turn prefetch applies a relevance/coverage gate, caps results and avoids repeating recently injected facts. Probe/reason actions provide entity-centered or compositional queries.

The default implementation is local. If optional embeddings or a cross-encoder reranker are configured, the README explicitly labels those paths online and says fact texts and query messages are sent to the named endpoint. Optional experience recording is also off by default and records which facts were emitted plus an agent-reported outcome; the source explicitly says emission does not prove the answer used a fact and outcomes are not human-verified.

metrics.evidence: Source describes FTS, multilingual matching, entity retrieval, scoring, and a prefetch relevance gate. No answerable/unanswerable workload or abstention outcome was scored.
Versioned updates, valid-time state, origin, and revert are source-visible. No correction accuracy or stale-value probe was run.
Fact and entity forgetting paths with keyed tombstones are present. No deletion-leak test was run, and external copies/backups were not evaluated.
Profile/user/chat/thread database scoping and missing-identity behavior are documented. No cross-user, chat, thread, or profile leakage workload was run.

Versions can record source and origin metadata and optional experience traces can identify emitted fact versions. The inspected provider does not establish answer-level citation support or entailment; no claims were adjudicated.
SQLite/FTS and bounded prefetch are source-visible. No runtime timing or write-to-recall samples were collected.
The README documents prefetch limits and optional online services; no token, cost, database-size, or storage-efficiency measurements were collected.

limits.text: Ranking and trust are retrieval heuristics, not a truth or entailment guarantee. Conflict detection is advisory; agent-provided origin and outcome signals can be inaccurate. Relevance gates and multilingual normalization may miss facts or admit unrelated ones, and no quality evaluation was performed here.

The default database is local, but optional embedding and reranking endpoints change the privacy boundary by receiving query and fact text. The README describes the configured scope identities and per-profile files; deployment-level filesystem permissions and real multi-user isolation were not tested.

No reviewed source or test was executed. Any README benchmark figures or synthetic examples remain upstream-reported and are not results for this assessment. Behavior of external memory providers and Hermes built-in memory is outside the Holographic store review.
